payload.claim: The post-repair-turn re-run (`after_repair`) handling at lines 3591-3594 mirrors the first re-run's abort/drift and probe-infra checks, but no test in this diff ever scripts the second gate re-run (the one right after the repair turn) with an `error` status or a drifted `tool`. Every suite used by the new b-0bd346 tests in test_session.py (`_GREEN_FORM_SUITE`, `_red_form_suite(...)`) only ever uses `pass`/`fail` statuses with a fixed `tool` string, so `after_repair.aborted` and `after_repair.drift` are always False in every scripted drive. Deleting the `if after_repair.aborted or after_repair.drift: return "GATE_ERROR"` check (so an aborted or drifted second re-run falls through to the `after_repair.new_failures` check and can be wrongly read as a passing re-run, routing a broken gate run to READY_FOR_REVIEW) would not make any existing or new test fail, even though the task's own problem statement (item 3) requires this case to be `GATE_ERROR` 'as today'.
